subject: Service Commitment Floor, Graceband Windows, and Credit Phasing
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@starlightai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@starlightai.com
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: baseline uptime, grace windows, and phased credits

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — we left excited about the latency profiles you showed. Before we move forward with a PO, procurement needs clarity on the SLA baseline and how credits would phase if we hit systematic performance degradations during our initial rollout. Two asks: 1) can Redwood commit to a 99.5% monthly uptime baseline for our production endpoint (we're in finance, so that bar is important), and 2) is there a way to avoid a cliff where a one-off incident in month 1 causes a full-month credit that skews our vendor spend model?

I've attached a marked-up SLA with our preferred wording and a simple monthly-credit model (spreadsheet). We're open to a phased approach during the first 90 days if that helps. Can you share the team's position and any suggested mitigation windows or 'gracebands' you might accept?

Elena Soto
VP of Infrastructure
Starlight AI

Attachments: starlight_proposed_sla_redline.pdf (PDF), monthly-credit-model.xlsx (Excel)
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@starlightai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: baseline uptime, grace windows, and phased credits

Elena — appreciate the clarity and the marked-up doc. Short answer: we can be pragmatic here.

High-level response:
- Standard hosted baseline: 99.9% monthly availability across the endpoint you use.
- For new customers onboarding at scale we can offer a 90-day ramp that smooths credit exposure ("phased credits"): reduced credit percentages for the first 30/60/90 days while we validate traffic patterns and warm caches.
- We are willing to discuss a narrowly scoped graceband for operational incidents that meet specific criteria (scheduled maintenance with 72h notice, provider-dependent transit outages we can trace, or incidents resolved within a short MTTR window). The graceband would not apply to repeat or prolonged outages.

I'll loop Laura (contracts) and Ben (customer success) to propose concrete language. Can you confirm whether the 99.5% is a hard requirement or a negotiable target for the first 90 days? Also, is the finance team expecting credits to be applied as a dollar credit or as a service credit (additional capacity / burst days)?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if that helps.

— Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@starlightai.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: baseline uptime, grace windows, and phased credits

Elena / team — looping in legal/contracts. A few contract-focused notes based on your redline:

1) Uptime baseline: our standard contractual commitment for hosted endpoints is 99.9% monthly. We can consider 99.5% for a defined ramp period, but that materially changes monthly credit exposure and will need clear guardrails.

2) Phased credits approach: we can adopt a stepped credit schedule for the first 90 days that caps Redwood's liability while still giving you meaningful remediation if there are systemic issues. Example (draft only): 0.5x credit for month 1 incidents, 0.75x month 2, 1.0x month 3+ for the same severity band. We need agreement on severity bands and how downtime is computed (per endpoint vs. per account).

3) Gracebands / exclusions: we can incorporate a short, narrowly defined operational graceband for the first onboarding month covering cache-warm issues and customer-side misconfigurations if you run a pre-production validation week. We will not accept open-ended 'provider transit' exclusions without telemetry to support them.

4) Credit form: we prefer credits against future invoices (financial credit) versus capacity allocations; however, we can make an exception for an initial onboarding credit pool if that's critical to your procurement model.

I'll prepare language for a redline and share a proposed schedule. Ben — can you add the expected onboarding SLOs and whether Starlight expects production traffic day-one?

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@starlightai.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: baseline uptime, grace windows, and phased credits

Elena — quick note from CS on ramp expectations and operational mitigations.

- Onboarding plan: if Starlight can run a two-week validation window against a staging endpoint with realistic traffic (we can provide a traffic replay tool), Redwood's ops team can proactively pre-warm caches and tune batching knobs. That materially reduces the risk of early incidents.
- Production day-one: if you expect full production immediately we will still offer the phased credit schedule but we will require an elevated monitoring and runbook review (we'll provide an onboarding checklist).
- Suggested phased credit tiers (draft):
  * Month 1: credit = 25% of the standard credit formula for qualifying incidents
  * Month 2: credit = 50%
  * Month 3+: credit = 100%

If Starlight prefers dollar credits instead of invoice offsets, we can model that in the attached spreadsheet and show the P&L impact. If you're open to the staging run, we can cut the Month 1 credit down to 10%.

Happy to review the redline once Laura posts one. If helpful, propose a 30-minute sync this week to finalize wording and close the PO.

Best,
Ben Carter
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@starlightai.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: baseline uptime, grace windows, and phased credits

Thanks all — that is very helpful. A few quick answers:
- 99.5% is our procurement team's preferred baseline for the first six months; they will accept a ramp but it's easier if you can commit to 99.5% with the phased credit schedule you described.
- The finance team wants credits as dollar invoice offsets rather than capacity tokens.
- We will run the two-week staging validation next week; we'll confirm dates by tomorrow.

Please proceed with Laura's redline and Ben's phased schedule (with the Month 1 = 25% proposal). We have a procurement cutoff on Friday, so a short sync this week would be ideal.

Elena
VP of Infrastructure, Starlight AI
